mainTopic: A husband's vow against his wife without a set time limit: the dispute between רב and שמואל, and who is to blame when a wife's vow is upheld
overview: This amud opens with the last words of an earlier discussion, which point to the incident of בית חורון. The גמרא then asks why רבי יהודה in the משנה seems to repeat the תנא קמא. אביי and רבא each explain what he adds. Next, רב and שמואל argue about a husband who makes a vow with no time limit. The גמרא explains why their argument had to appear in two different משניות. It then challenges שמואל from the case of a vow against tasting a fruit. To defend him, it says the wife made the vow and the husband upheld it, which leads to a long rearranging of the names in a ברייתא about who is to blame for an unrevoked vow. Finally, the גמרא starts a new contradiction about whether רבי יוסי holds that a husband can cancel a vow about adorning, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The incident of בית חורון closes the earlier discussion
steps.stepSummary: These are the closing words of the previous discussion. They name the incident of בית חורון as the source of רבי יוסי's concern about tricks used to get around a vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: (רבי יוסי is concerned because of) the incident of בית חורון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its earlier discussion by pointing to a famous story, the incident of בית חורון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that story, a man used a gift to get around a vow, and the plan went wrong. Because of it, רבי יוסי is worried about any trick that sidesteps a vow, while the חכמים are not worried.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident or story that happened
A place name; the 'incident of בית חורון' is a well-known story about getting around a vow

phrases.english: The incident of Beit Choron.
phrases.notes: These words finish the sentence from before: רבי יוסי is worried because of what happened in בית חורון.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעֲשֶׂה דְּבֵית חוֹרוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the discussion from the previous page about רבי יוסי and the חכמים.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוסי's concern about tricks to get around a vow comes from the incident of בית חורון.

steps.title: Quoting רבי יהודה's view in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה from the משנה. For an ordinary ישראל, a vow lasting one month allows the marriage to continue.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: for a ישראל, one month (he may keep her), and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting רבי יהודה's words from the משנה. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא said that if the vow lasts up to thirty days, the husband appoints a middleman to support her. רבי יהודה says that for a ישראל, one month is allowed. For a כהן he allows two months.

keyTerms.meaning: An ordinary Jew who is not a כהן
One month
'And so on'; the rest of the quote is assumed

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
For an Israelite, one month, etc.
phrases.notes: The full משנה goes on: two months for a ישראל means divorce, and a כהן's wife gets one month more.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל חֹדֶשׁ אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: analyzing רבי יהודה in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a ישראל, a vow lasting one month allows the marriage to continue. For a כהן, two months.

steps.title: Isn't this the same as the first opinion?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה is needed. One month sounds the same as the תנא קמא's thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the same as the first תנא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רבי יהודה's rule for a ישראל looks identical to the תנא קמא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Thirty days and one month seem to be the same length of time. So רבי יהודה does not appear to be arguing. The challenge is: what is he adding?

keyTerms.meaning: 'That is the same as'
The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Even though this is phrased as a question, it is really a challenge. It asks why רבי יהודה needs to speak at all if he says nothing new.

phrases.english: This is the same as the first tanna!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְינוּ תַּנָּא קַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the רבי יהודה quote from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's statement about a ישראל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One month equals thirty days, so his view seems to repeat the תנא קמא.

steps.title: אביי: רבי יהודה adds the rule for a כהן's wife
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that רבי יהודה agrees with the תנא קמא about a ישראל. His new point is the extra time given in the case of a כהן's wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: he came to teach us about the wife of a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge. רבי יהודה mentions the ישראל only as a lead-in, and his real addition is the rule for a כהנת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אביי, there is no argument about a ישראל at all. רבי יהודה's new teaching is that a כהן gets two months. A כהן cannot remarry his wife after a divorce, so more time is given before forcing one.

keyTerms.meaning: The wife of a כהן
'He came to teach us'

phrases.english: Abaye said:
He came to teach us about the wife of a priest.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: כֹּהֶנֶת אֲתָא לְאַשְׁמוֹעִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Admits there is no argument about a ישראל and finds the new point elsewhere
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה seemed to add nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: His addition is the extra time for a כהנת.

steps.title: רבא: a full month versus a short month
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives another answer. The two views really do differ, depending on whether the month is full or short.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the difference between them is a full month and a short month.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a different answer from אביי. He says there is a real practical difference between the two views about a ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא means exactly thirty days. רבי יהודה says 'one month,' which also includes a short month of twenty-nine days. So the two views give different results when the month is short.

keyTerms.meaning: A full month of thirty days
A short month of twenty-nine days
'The difference between them is'

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers to 'Isn't this the same as the תנא קמא?' אביי says the new point is the כהנת. רבא says the views differ over a full month versus a short month.

phrases.english: Rava said:
A full month and a deficient month
is the difference between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: חֹדֶשׁ מָלֵא וְחֹדֶשׁ חָסֵר אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 3, different from אביי's.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finds a practical difference between the two views
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Thirty days and one month seemed identical.
steps.terutzMaskana: They differ in a short month of twenty-nine days.

steps.title: רב: the time limits apply only when he sets a time
steps.stepSummary: רב says the משנה's time limits apply only when the husband states how long the vow will last. If he gives no time limit, he must divorce her right away and pay her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: they taught this only when he specified a time. But if he did not specify, he must divorce her immediately and pay the כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new discussion. רב limits the משנה's rule to a vow with a stated time limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the husband says how long the vow will last, we can wait out that time. If he says nothing, the vow could last forever. So רב says the husband must divorce her immediately and pay her כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They taught this only'; used to narrow a rule
He specified a time limit
Unspecified; with no time limit
Immediately

phrases.english: Rav said:
They taught this only where he specifies,
phrases.notes: He means the man stated how long the vow would last.

phrases.english: but in an unspecified case,
he must divorce her immediately and give her the marriage contract payment.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בִּמְפָרֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new discussion about the משנה's case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the vow has no stated time limit, he must divorce her immediately and pay her כתובה.

steps.title: שמואל: even without a time limit, do not rush the divorce
steps.stepSummary: שמואל disagrees with רב. Even if no time was stated, the husband should not divorce her right away, because he may find a way to have the vow undone.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: even if he did not specify, he should not divorce her, because perhaps he will find an opening to undo his vow.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל argues with רב about the vow with no time limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חכם can undo a vow if there is a good reason, which is called a פתח. Since the husband might still find such a reason, שמואל does not force an immediate divorce.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps
'An opening'; a reason that lets a חכם undo a vow
A vow

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
Even in an unspecified case he should not divorce her,
perhaps he will find an opening for his vow.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ בִּסְתָם לֹא יוֹצִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even with no time limit, there is no immediate divorce, since the vow may still be undone.

steps.title: They already argued about this once before
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that רב and שמואל already had this argument about another משנה. That משנה deals with a vow forbidding marital relations.
steps.simpleTranslation: But they already argued about this once! As we learned: if a man vows to forbid his wife from marital relations, בית שמאי say two weeks and בית הלל say one week.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the repetition. It brings the earlier משנה where רב and שמואל first argued about this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier משנה, the vow forbids marital relations, and the time limits are one or two weeks. The same question arises there: what if the husband sets no time limit? The next step shows that רב and שמואל already argued about it there.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But they already argued about it'
One time
One who forbids someone by a vow
Marital relations

phrases.english: But they already disagreed about it one time,
as we learned in a mishna:
One who vows, forbidding his wife from marital relations,
Beit Shammai say: two weeks.
And Beit Hillel say: one week.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אִיפְּלִגוּ בַּיהּ חֲדָא זִימְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the רב and שמואל argument in steps 6 and 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The repeated argument between רב and שמואל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If they already argued about the same issue in another משנה, saying it again seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The earlier argument between רב and שמואל, word for word
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רב and שמואל on the earlier משנה. Their argument there is the same as the one here.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב said: the argument is when he specified, but if unspecified, he must divorce her immediately and pay the כתובה. And שמואל said: even if unspecified he should not divorce her, because perhaps he will find an opening to undo his vow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its challenge. It shows that רב and שמואל said the very same words about the earlier משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording is almost identical; only מחלוקת replaces לא שנו, and נמי is added. Since their argument already appears there, the challenge is why it is repeated here. The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: The argument or dispute
Also

steps.whatToRemember: רב and שמואל argue about a vow with no time limit in two different משניות. The גמרא is about to explain why both are needed.

phrases.english: And Rav said:
The dispute is where he specifies,
but in an unspecified case,
he must divorce her immediately and give her the marriage contract payment.
And Shmuel said:
Even in an unspecified case he also should not divorce her,
perhaps he will find an opening for his vow.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב: מַחְלוֹקֶת בִּמְפָרֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge from step 8 by quoting the earlier argument.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need to repeat the argument between רב and שמואל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Their words on the earlier משנה are the same, so the second statement seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Why the argument had to be stated twice
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that both arguments of רב and שמואל are needed. In one case a פרנס can solve the problem, and in the other case he cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is necessary to say it twice. If they had argued only about the vow forbidding marital relations, we might think רב says divorce right away only there, because a trustee cannot help. But here, where a trustee can provide for her, we might think רב agrees with שמואל. And if they had argued only here, we might think שמואל says not to divorce only here, because a trustee can help. But there, we might think he agrees with רב. So both are necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Steps 8-9: why do we need רב and שמואל to argue in two places? It says each case has something special about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the vow against benefiting from the husband, a trustee (פרנס) can give her support, so there is less reason to divorce her right away. In the vow forbidding marital relations, no trustee can help. If we only had one argument, we might think the other rabbi agrees in the other case.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary (both statements are needed)
A trustee or go-between who supports her so she does not benefit directly from the husband
Agrees, admits
I might say, one might think

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic צריכא answer. When the same argument appears twice, the גמרא shows that each case could have been seen differently.

phrases.english: It is necessary,
for if it had been stated only in that case:
phrases.notes: "That case" is the vow forbidding marital relations, from Steps 8-9.

phrases.english: in that case Rav says (divorce right away)
because it cannot be solved through a trustee,
but in this case, which can be solved through a trustee,
I might say he agrees with Shmuel.
And if it had been stated only in this case:
in this case Shmuel says (do not divorce)
because it can be solved through a trustee,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּהַהִיא, אֵימָא מוֹדֶה לֵיהּ לְרַב
phrases.english: but in that case, I might say he agrees with Rav.
So it is necessary.

steps.triggerLanguage: צְרִיכָא, דְּאִי אִיתְּמַר בְּהָהִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Steps 8-9 about why the argument is repeated.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכא: each case has its own reason, so both are needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The argument appears twice for no reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: Without both statements, we might think each rabbi agrees with the other in the other case, because a פרנס helps in one case but not the other.

steps.title: The fruit-tasting case challenges שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a husband who forbids his wife from tasting a kind of fruit must divorce her and pay her כתובה. This fits רב, but seems to go against שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: one who makes his wife vow not to taste any one kind of fruit must divorce her and give her the כתובה. This works well for רב: here the vow has no time limit, and there (the first case) a time limit was given. But for שמואל it is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next case in the משנה and uses it to challenge שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says to divorce right away with no time limit mentioned. רב can explain this: when no time is stated, he must divorce right away. But שמואל said even without a time limit we should wait, since he may get the vow undone, so this line seems to contradict him.

keyTerms.meaning: One who places a vow on someone else
Unspecified, with no time limit stated
Specifying, stating a time limit
Granted, this works well (for one view)

phrases.english: We learned:
One who places a vow on his wife
that she may not taste any one kind of fruit
must divorce her and give her the ketubah.
Granted, according to Rav:
here it is unspecified, there it is specified.
phrases.notes: "Here" is this fruit case, and "there" is the earlier case in the משנה with time limits.

phrases.english: But according to Shmuel, it is difficult!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: הַמַּדִּיר אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new challenge, now against שמואל's view from Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that even with no time limit he should not divorce right away.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה rules 'divorce and pay' in a case with no stated time limit, which is exactly what רב said and what שמואל denied.

steps.title: The case is where she made the vow and he upheld it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers for שמואל: the משנה is talking about a vow the wife made herself, which the husband upheld. רבי מאיר holds that by upholding it, the husband is responsible.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here we are dealing with a case where she made the vow, and he upheld it. And רבי מאיר holds that he has put his finger between her teeth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל by explaining the fruit case in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since she made the vow herself, she will not look for a way to undo it, so there is no point waiting and he must divorce now. He still pays the כתובה because, by upholding her vow, he is the one who made it stick. This משנה is being read as following רבי מאיר's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Here what are we dealing with? (introduces a narrower case)
Upheld, confirmed (a vow, instead of canceling it)
Puts a finger between her teeth: causes the vow to take hold, so he is responsible

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up who is responsible here. In this answer the husband is blamed ("he put his finger"), even though the wife made the vow.

phrases.english: Here, what case are we dealing with?
Such as where she made the vow,
and he upheld it for her.
And Rabbi Meir holds
that he puts a finger between her teeth.
phrases.notes: It's a picture: he put his finger in her mouth, so he can't complain when it gets bitten. He's the one who let the vow stand.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן כְּגוֹן שֶׁנָּדְרָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against שמואל in Step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is about a vow the husband placed on her with no time limit, which goes against שמואל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about her own vow that he upheld. She won't undo it, so he divorces now, and he pays because רבי מאיר holds he is responsible.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows רבי מאיר blames the wife
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim about רבי מאיר. In a ברייתא, רבי מאיר says that when a wife's vow is not canceled, she is the one who "put her finger between her teeth," and she leaves without a כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי מאיר really hold that he puts a finger between her teeth? But a ברייתא teaches: a woman who vowed to be a נזירה, and her husband heard and did not cancel it, רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה say: she put her finger between her own teeth. Therefore, if the husband wants to cancel it, he may cancel it. And if he says, "I do not want a wife who makes vows," she leaves without her כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of Step 12 by quoting a ברייתא where רבי מאיר seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 said רבי מאיר blames the husband when he upholds her vow, so he must pay the כתובה. But in this ברייתא רבי מאיר blames the wife, and she gets no כתובה. So the answer for שמואל seems to fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: One who vows to avoid wine, haircuts, and contact with the dead
Canceled (a vow, by the husband)
A woman who makes vows often
Without her כתובה payment

steps.whyThisMatters: The whole defense of שמואל depends on how רבי מאיר assigns blame. So this contradiction must be resolved for שמואל's view to hold up.

phrases.english: And does Rabbi Meir hold
that he puts a finger between her teeth?
But it was taught:
A woman who made a vow to be a nazirite,
and her husband heard and did not cancel it for her,
Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda say:
She put a finger between her own teeth,

phrases.aramaic: לְפִיכָךְ אִם רָצָה הַבַּעַל לְהָפֵר — יָפֵר.
phrases.english: therefore, if the husband wants to cancel it, he may cancel it.
And if he said:
"I do not want a wife who makes vows,"
she leaves without her ketubah.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר הוּא נוֹתֵן אֶצְבַּע בֵּין שִׁינֶּיהָ? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim about רבי מאיר that Step 12's answer relied on.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 12's claim that רבי מאיר holds the husband responsible when he upholds his wife's vow.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא quotes רבי מאיר saying the wife is responsible ("she put her finger between her teeth") and leaves without a כתובה, which is the opposite of what Step 12 needed.

steps.title: The other side of the ברייתא: the husband is responsible
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: רבי יוסי and רבי אלעזר say the husband 'puts his finger between her teeth,' so if he divorces her he must pay her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי and רבי אלעזר say: He puts his finger between her teeth. So if the husband wants to cancel the vow, he may cancel it. And if he says, 'I don't want a wife who makes vows,' he must divorce her and give her the כתובה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא from the last step. This second half shows that the opposite view, that the husband is responsible, belongs to רבי יוסי and רבי אלעזר, not to רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the attack on שמואל is complete. שמואל needed רבי מאיר to hold that a husband who leaves his wife's vow in place is responsible. This ברייתא gives that view to רבי יוסי and רבי אלעזר, and puts רבי מאיר on the other side.

keyTerms.meaning: Putting a finger between her teeth: being the one who caused the problem
To cancel a vow (a husband's power over his wife's vows)
A wife who makes vows

steps.confusionAlert: 'He puts a finger between her teeth' means the husband is to blame, because he could have canceled the vow and didn't. So he pays the כתובה. 'She put' means she is to blame, so she gets nothing.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Elazar say:
He is putting a finger between her teeth,

phrases.aramaic: לְפִיכָךְ אִם רָצָה הַבַּעַל לְהָפֵר — יָפֵר.
phrases.english: therefore, if the husband wants to cancel it, he may cancel it.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אָמַר: אִי אֶפְשִׁי בְּאִשָּׁה נַדְרָנִית
phrases.english: And if he said: I do not want a wife who makes vows,
he must divorce her and give her the כתובה!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמְרִים: הוּא נוֹתֵן אֶצְבַּע בֵּין שִׁינֶּיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא quote begun in Step 13, which completes the challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 12 that רבי מאיר holds the husband responsible when he upholds his wife's vow.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא gives the 'husband is responsible' view to רבי יוסי and רבי אלעזר, which implies רבי מאיר holds the opposite.

steps.title: Swap the names in the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by reversing the ברייתא: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה say the husband is responsible, and רבי יוסי and רבי אלעזר say the wife is.
steps.simpleTranslation: Reverse it: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה say, 'He puts,' and רבי יוסי and רבי אלעזר say, 'She put.'
steps.whatsHappening: To save שמואל, the גמרא says the names in the ברייתא should be flipped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the names are switched, רבי מאיר holds that the husband is responsible, exactly as שמואל needed in Step 12. The cost is that רבי יוסי and רבי אלעזר now hold that the wife is responsible.

keyTerms.meaning: Reverse it: switch which רבנים hold which opinion
She put (her own finger between her teeth): she is to blame

phrases.english: Reverse it,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמְרִים: הוּא נוֹתֵן,
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda say: He is putting,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמְרִים: הִיא נָתְנָה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Elazar say: She put.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיפוֹךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא by switching the names.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reversing the opinions in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא as quoted puts רבי מאיר on the side that the wife is responsible.
steps.terutzMaskana: The correct reading has רבי מאיר holding that the husband is responsible, which fits שמואל.

steps.title: But רבי יוסי in our משנה holds the husband responsible
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the swap. In our משנה, רבי יוסי says that for poor women, when no time limit is set, he must divorce her and pay. That means he holds the husband responsible.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי יוסי really hold 'she put'? But we learned in the משנה: רבי יוסי says, 'For poor women, when he did not set a time limit' (he must divorce her and pay the כתובה)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new reading. It points to a משנה where רבי יוסי seems to blame the husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to שמואל, the משניות here are about a vow the wife made and the husband upheld. Since רבי יוסי makes the husband pay in such a case, he must hold 'he puts.' That contradicts the swapped ברייתא, which puts רבי יוסי on the 'she put' side.

keyTerms.meaning: Poor women
A set time limit

phrases.english: And does Rabbi Yosei hold that she put?
But didn't we learn: Rabbi Yosei says:
For poor women, when he did not set a time limit!
phrases.notes: This is from the משנה about a vow against wearing a certain perfume. In that case he must divorce her and pay the כתובה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הִיא נָתְנָה? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reversed reading from Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: Placing רבי יוסי on the 'she put' side.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Following שמואל's reading of the משנה, רבי יוסי makes the husband pay for a vow he upheld, so he must hold 'he puts.'

steps.title: Re-pair the names: רבי מאיר with רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rearranges again: רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי say the husband is responsible, and רבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר say the wife is.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי say, 'He puts,' and רבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר say, 'She put.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the problem with רבי יוסי by moving him to the 'husband is responsible' side together with רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי both fit שמואל. But רבי יהודה has been moved to the 'she put' side, and that sets up the next challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Say: read the text this way instead

phrases.aramaic: אֵימָא, רַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמְרִים: הוּא נוֹתֵן,
phrases.english: Say: Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yosei say: He is putting,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמְרִים: הִיא נָתְנָה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Elazar say: She put.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא, רַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמְרִים: הוּא נוֹתֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 16 by re-pairing the names.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rearranging the names in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי was paired with רבי אלעזר on the 'she put' side.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי is paired with רבי מאיר on the 'he puts' side.

steps.title: But רבי יהודה in our משנה also holds the husband responsible
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again. In the fruit-tasting clause of the משנה (Step 11), רבי יהודה says that for the wife of a ישראל, a vow lasting one day lets the husband keep her, and if it lasts longer he must divorce her and pay. That shows he blames the husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי יהודה really hold 'she put'? But we learned in the משנה: רבי יהודה says, 'For a Jewish woman, one day: he may keep her!'
steps.whatsHappening: The new arrangement is challenged because רבי יהודה, now on the 'she put' side, seems in our משנה to hold the husband responsible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Following שמואל, the משנה is about a vow the wife made that the husband upheld. רבי יהודה makes the husband pay if the vow goes on longer, so he must hold 'he puts.' This is the same kind of challenge as Step 16, now aimed at רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: He may keep her (stay married to her)
For a regular Jewish woman (as opposed to a כהן's wife)

phrases.english: And does Rabbi Yehuda hold that she put?
But didn't we learn: Rabbi Yehuda says:
For an Israelite woman, one day, he may keep her!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא נָתְנָה? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the new arrangement from Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: Placing רבי יהודה on the 'she put' side.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Following שמואל's reading of the משנה, רבי יהודה makes the husband pay for a vow he upheld, so he must hold 'he puts.'

steps.title: Three against one: only רבי אלעזר blames the wife
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rearranges once more: רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי all say the husband is responsible, and only רבי אלעזר says the wife is.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי say, 'He puts,' and רבי אלעזר says, 'She put.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא puts all three רבנים whose views appear in our משניות on the 'husband is responsible' side. Only רבי אלעזר is left on the other side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This removes every contradiction. רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי all match what they say in the משניות as שמואל reads them. The only odd thing is that the ברייתא now has three against one instead of two pairs.

phrases.english: Say: Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda
and Rabbi Yosei say: He is putting,
and Rabbi Elazar says: She put.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא, רַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמְרִים: הוּא נוֹתֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 18 by moving רבי יהודה to the 'he puts' side too.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rearranging the names into three against one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה was on the 'she put' side.
steps.terutzMaskana: All three רבנים from the משניות hold 'he puts'; only רבי אלעזר holds 'she put.'

steps.title: If the ברייתא must have pairs, put רבי מאיר with רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: If the ברייתא always lists the רבנים in pairs, then read it as: רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר say the wife is responsible, and רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי say the husband is.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say the ברייתא teaches the רבנים in pairs, then say: רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר say, 'She put,' and רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי say, 'He puts.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second option for anyone who insists the ברייתא must have two pairs. In this option, רבי מאיר goes back to the 'she put' side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With pairs, רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי must stay on the 'he puts' side because of Steps 16 and 18. That forces רבי מאיר to join רבי אלעזר on the 'she put' side. This leaves a problem for the unnamed משנה, which the next line deals with.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want to say (introduces another possible answer)
It is taught in pairs (two רבנים on each side)

phrases.english: And if you say
it is taught in pairs,
phrases.notes: The ברייתא lists two רבנים on each side, so three against one wouldn't fit its style.

phrases.aramaic: אֵימָא, רַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמְרִים: הִיא נָתְנָה,
phrases.english: say: Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Elazar say: She put,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמְרִים: הוּא נוֹתֵן.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yosei say: He is putting.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם תִּמְצָא לוֹמַר זוּגֵי זוּגֵי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different arrangement in case the three-against-one reading of Step 19 is rejected.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative arrangement that keeps the pairs
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Three against one breaks the ברייתא's pattern of pairs.
steps.terutzMaskana: Keep the pairs: רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר hold 'she put,' and רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי hold 'he puts.'

steps.title: Then the unnamed משנה does not follow רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: With this second arrangement, the unnamed משנה (that the husband must divorce her and pay) does not match רבי מאיר, and the גמרא accepts that.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this unnamed משנה is simply not like רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits the result of the pairs option: the unnamed משנה from Step 11 is not following רבי מאיר. It accepts this, and the defense of שמואל holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 12, שמואל's answer relied on the משנה being רבי מאיר. Under the pairs reading, רבי מאיר holds 'she put,' so the unnamed משנה, which makes the husband pay, must follow a different תנא. The גמרא treats this as acceptable, so שמואל is still defended.

keyTerms.meaning: An unnamed (anonymous) ruling in a משנה

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא defends שמואל by rearranging the names in the ברייתא. Either three רבנים (רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי) hold that the husband is responsible, or, if the ברייתא must be in pairs, רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי hold it, and the unnamed משנה simply does not follow רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: And this unnamed ruling is not in accordance with Rabbi Meir.
phrases.notes: He means the unnamed משנה about forbidding a fruit, which makes the husband divorce her and pay the כתובה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא סְתָמָא דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: States and accepts what follows from the pairs arrangement in Step 20.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Under the pairs reading, the unnamed משנה follows a תנא other than רבי מאיר, and שמואל's explanation still stands.

steps.title: Does רבי יוסי hold that a husband can cancel a vow about adorning?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws an inference from רבי יוסי's ruling about poor women: it seems he holds that a husband can cancel his wife's vow not to adorn herself.
steps.simpleTranslation: And does רבי יוסי really hold that for poor women, when the husband did not set a time limit, he must divorce her? That would mean a husband can cancel this kind of vow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out what רבי יוסי's ruling in our משנה seems to imply. This is a setup: it prepares the contradiction that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We now read the משנה as a case where the wife made the vow and the husband let it stand. If רבי יוסי blames the husband for that, it must be because the husband had the power to cancel it. So רבי יוסי must hold that a vow about adorning is one a husband can cancel.

keyTerms.meaning: Apparently / this shows that
To cancel a vow (from הֲפָרָה, a husband's power to cancel his wife's vow)

steps.confusionAlert: This step is not a ruling. It is an inference the גמרא draws so that it can challenge it in the next step.

phrases.english: And does Rabbi Yosei hold
regarding poor women, that when he did not set a time limit [he must divorce her],
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוסי's ruling in our משנה about a vow not to adorn herself.

phrases.english: this shows that a husband can cancel [this vow]?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the reading that the wife vowed and the husband let it stand, and draws out what that means for רבי יוסי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יוסי truly holds that a husband can cancel a wife's vow about adorning.

steps.title: Contradiction from the משנה in נדרים about vows of affliction
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה where רבי יוסי says vows about bathing and adorning are not vows of affliction, so it seems a husband cannot cancel them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they raised a contradiction: These are the vows a husband can cancel: vows that cause affliction, like 'If I bathe,' 'If I do not bathe,' 'If I adorn myself,' 'If I do not adorn myself.' רבי יוסי said: These are not vows of affliction. These are vows of affliction: 'That I will not eat meat,' 'That I will not drink wine,' 'That I will not adorn myself...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה from נדרים that seems to say the opposite about רבי יוסי. There, רבי יוסי says a vow about adorning is not a vow of affliction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband can cancel his wife's vows only if they are vows of affliction (עינוי נפש), or certain other types. The first opinion lists bathing and adorning as vows of affliction, but רבי יוסי says they are not. His own list does include a narrower kind of adorning, and his sentence finishes on the next amud. So how could רבי יוסי in our משנה hold that the husband could cancel her vow not to adorn herself in a certain way?

keyTerms.meaning: And they raised a contradiction (two sources that seem to clash)
Affliction of the self; a vow that causes the woman to suffer, which a husband can cancel
Vows of
I will adorn myself

steps.whyThisMatters: The whole question is whether a vow about adorning is something a husband can cancel. That decides whether the husband is to blame in our משנה.

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
These are the vows that the husband can cancel:
vows that involve affliction of the self,
"If I bathe," "If I do not bathe."
phrases.notes: These are short forms of vowing off bathing. Either way, she ends up not bathing.

phrases.english: "If I adorn myself," "If I do not adorn myself."
Rabbi Yosei said:
These are not vows of affliction,
but these are the vows of affliction:
"That I will not eat meat," and "That I will not drink wine,"
and "That I will not adorn myself

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְמִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference from step 22 by quoting a source where רבי יוסי seems to hold the opposite.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that רבי יוסי holds a husband can cancel a vow about adorning.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the משנה in נדרים, רבי יוסי says bathing and adorning vows are not vows of affliction. A husband can cancel only vows of affliction (or certain other types), so it seems the husband could not cancel this vow. That clashes with our משנה.
